successors.name: Anga
successors.text: Anga between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east, capital at Champa/Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger; south of Vajji, Ganga plain with Banka-Godda uplands

ledger.x: c. 1100 BCE: the kingdom of Anga stands on the middle Ganges. Infobox 'Established: Unknown (~1100 BCE)', 'Historical era: Iron Age', 'Aṅga and other kingdoms of the late Vedic period'. The page dates nothing else before the 6th century, so the whole early life is traditional.

c. 600 BCE: the Anga of the Vedic and Jain tradition becomes the janapada of Anga. The page has no event for the date; it is the Mahajanapada convention year of the sa-01-a dossier, and 'During the 6th century BCE, the king of Anga was Dadhivahana'.
